snip.t: This elevated pressure is due to a combination of increased pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR), increased pulmonary blood flow, and/or increased left atrial pressure.

Pulmonary vasculature (arterioles & veins) – thin‑walled muscular vessels: Fibrotic distortion narrows vessels, raising pulmonary vascular resistance → secondary pulmonary hypertension and right‑heart strain (cor pulmonale).
It often appears after a few days, once the pulmonary vascular resistance falls.
Chronic increases in pulmonary vascular resistance lead to RV hypertrophy and eventual dilatation and failure.
Used in evaluating pulmonary vascular resistance and preoperative Coronary artery disease assessment
Usually asymptomatic at neonatal period;\n● Due to high pulmonary vascular resistance\n● Baby may have slightly lower oxygen saturation

AVSD
• Clinical Features:
• Usually asymptomatic at neonatal period
– Due to high pulmonary vascular resistance
– Baby may have slightly lower oxygen saturation
Eisenmenger syndrome — determined by pulmonary vascular resistance
